belief: Being raised in a Christian family makes me a Christian.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that being raised in a Christian family makes you a Christian, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Growing up in church and always identifying as a Christian. Being baptized or confirmed as a child without understanding it. Parents or grandparents with strong faith. A culture where being Christian is part of family or national identity. Never being asked whether you personally trust Christ.
teaches: A Christian family is a great blessing, and God often uses parents to plant faith in children. But each person must personally receive Christ. To all who receive Him and believe in His name, God gives the right to become His children, born not of human descent but of God. Jesus said no one can see the kingdom of God unless he is born again. John the Baptist warned people not to rely on having Abraham as their father. Faith cannot be inherited; it must be your own.
self_statements: I’ve always gone to church, so I’m fine.
I was baptized as a baby, so I don’t need anything else.
My family name speaks for me.
I don’t need a personal relationship with Jesus.
errors: Taking your faith for granted without examining it.
Treating a family or cultural label as a personal faith.
Relying on someone else’s relationship with God.
Not asking the question because you fear the answer.
questions: Who does John 1:12 say becomes a child of God?
What did Jesus mean by “born again”?
If my parents had no faith, would I still believe?
Have I ever personally trusted Christ, or just grown up around Him?
What does Romans 10:9 say I must do?
Is my faith my own or borrowed?
What would it mean to make my family’s faith my own?
truth: Being raised in a Christian family is a blessing, but it does not make me a Christian. I become God’s child by personally receiving Jesus and believing in His name. My faith must be my own. I can thank God for my family’s faith and personally put my trust in Christ.
hw_questions: Who becomes a child of God?
What does “born again” mean for me?
Would I believe if my parents didn’t?
What does Romans 10:9 ask of me?

hw_truths: I become God’s child by receiving Jesus personally.
My faith must be my own, not inherited.
God has no grandchildren, only children.
A Christian family is a blessing, not a substitute.
I can personally trust Christ today.
If I confess Jesus as Lord and believe, I am saved.
log: Each day, write one thing I personally believe about Jesus and why.
name_example: But to Sarah, who did receive Him and believed in His name, He gave the right to become a child of God.

prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for the people who taught me about You. Help me reject the lie that being raised in a Christian family makes me a Christian. I personally receive You and believe in Your name. Make my faith my own, and help me follow You for the rest of my life. In Your name, Amen.
